# VMFS reader origin

This is LovelyCarve's read-only Rust implementation, licensed AGPL-3.0-only. The VMware LVM records, descriptor fields, block address encodings and VMFS 6 directory allocation format were checked against Fox-IT's [dissect.vmfs](https://github.com/fox-it/dissect.vmfs/tree/0a385a1d80f5881f73402b7b847305dc478eae1c) at `0a385a1d80f5881f73402b7b847305dc478eae1c` (AGPL-3.0-or-later). Broadcom's [VMFS volume documentation](https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/309687/manually-creating-a-vmfs-volume-using-vm.html) was consulted for terminology. The Rust implementation uses bounded `Read + Seek` sources and does not bundle upstream Python code, tools, or test images.

The upstream GitHub source archive for the pinned commit has SHA-256 `ccbab7c5eb3c0d73cc545f902105d8b752e1f5294ebcc7a4f97e9795d2d94e2a`. Obtain each image from the same revision's official Git LFS endpoint, `https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/fox-it/dissect.vmfs/<revision>/tests/_data/vmfs/<name>.bin.gz`. Check the compressed size and SHA-256 against the matching [LFS pointer](https://github.com/fox-it/dissect.vmfs/tree/0a385a1d80f5881f73402b7b847305dc478eae1c/tests/_data/vmfs) before decompressing. Preserve `span/` and point `LOVELYCARVE_VMFS_ORACLE` at the resulting `vmfs/` directory. The raw images expand to several GiB each and can be extracted as sparse files.

The ignored Rust tests verify logical-to-physical offsets and bytes on VMFS 5, VMFS 6, VMFS-L, direct logical volumes and optimized metadata layouts. File data and allocated names are checked against the upstream Python implementation and tests. The CLI oracle also uses the independent reader's `.fdc.sf` bytes on both members of each assembled datastore.
